newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close sharply down, index below 14,000.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close sharply down, index below 14,000.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks nose dived on Thursday and the Hang Seng Index closed below 14,000 for the first time since May 13 as sentiment turned bearish on concerns about local property and China's stock markets, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index plunged 497.18 points, or 3.45 percent, to finish at 13,924.34. Turnover was HK$17.43 billion compared to HK$17.51 billion on Wednesday.
"Major brokerages turned bearish on Hong Kong stocks, some funds are seen unloading their holdings and sentiment as a whole is weak," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.
Property stocks led the fall with Henderson Land easing HK$3.25 at HK$65.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties dropping HK$3.50 to HK$86.00.
HSBC also tumbled HK$6.00 to HK$227.00.
"The Chinese are cracking down on liquidity in their markets, which affected their markets and our market," said Archie Hart, associate director at BZW Securities Asia.

"People are getting more concerned about the property side of things, also signs that regulators are getting more serious in Hong Kong and I think some of the speculators have been hurt quite badly in the last few days," he added.
Beijing has recently announced a series of measures, including a ban on state banks investing in stock markets, aimed at calming China's exuberant bourses.
Analysts also said buyers were taking a pause to wait for new Hong Kong government measures, probably due in the next few weeks, to curb rising local property prices.

Second- and third-line stocks bore the brunt of selling on fears that regulators were clamping down on speculation, brokers said. The stock exchange said earlier this week that trading suspensions of 11 stocks were due to enquiries into "unusual trading movement", the first time it made such an announcement.
Pearl Oriental plunged HK$0.62, or 35.84 percent, to close at HK$1.11.
The company issued a statement denying rumours of a possible probe into its share price movement by Hong Kong stock regulators and of financial difficulties.
Among red chips, Beijing Enterprises was down HK$4.10 to HK$41.70 and Shanghai Industrial slumped HK$2.10 at HK$39.80.
Brokers said the next support level for the Hang Seng index was likely to be at 13,500, a 50 percent pullback from the peak of its recent rally which started from April.
